{{Hatnote|For the 2006 Players Committee printable slips, see [[Virtual Set: Defensive Shields|Defensive Shields]].}}
[[File:Ref3-D-fearismyally.gif|thumb|right|200px|[[Fear Is My Ally]], Dark Starting Effect.]]
'''Silver bullets''' (also called '''teching''') are [[Star Wars CCG]] cards printed to counter other cards and strategies.<ref name="teching-def" /> [[Decipher]] used them so that no one deck stayed the best deck, and so the game would not need a banned list.<ref name="teching-def" /><ref name="path-ban" /><ref name="rfd02" /> The printed line grew from specific interrupts in the 60-card deck into start-of-game Effects. [[Reflections III: A Collector's Bounty]] then moved many of those counters onto [[Defensive Shield]]s played from a side pile.<ref name="ref3-rules" /><ref name="colson-shields" />

== No banned list ==
Decipher's policy was to fix problem cards, not ban them.<ref name="rfd02" /> In 1998 the designers said the only card Decipher had ever banned was from ''Star Trek'' Premiere: "We want to make sure that every card you have, you can play."<ref name="rfd02" /> See [[Design of Star Wars CCG]].

''A Path Unlike Any Other'' says Star Wars CCG has no restricted list and no banned list.<ref name="path-ban" /> It says Decipher wanted to stay different from ''Magic: The Gathering'' on that point.<ref name="path-ban" /><ref name="teching-def" /> Overpowered cards and strategies instead got silver bullets.<ref name="path-ban" />

[[Jim Colson]] said the options were banning cards or issuing a mountain of [[errata]].<ref name="colson-shields" /> The first formal errata was a picture, then [[Asteroid Sanctuary]].<ref name="colson-shields" /> Physical replacement cards brought in "Nada. Zero. Nilch" in revenue.<ref name="colson-shields" /> He said Decipher did not have the stomach for massive errata.<ref name="colson-shields" />

== Early counters ==
[[Monnok]] and [[Grimtaash]] punish a large hand and duplicate copies in hand.<ref name="teching-monnok" /> A deck of many copies of one unique character is legal. Those two cards make that plan risky.<ref name="teching-monnok" />

[[Disarmed]] is a counter to a character holding a weapon. It also shuts off cards that need a weapon, such as [[Lightsaber Proficiency]].<ref name="teching-disarmed" /> Undercover spies stop Force drains at those sites. Later cards then counter the spies, and further cards counter those counters.<ref name="teching-uc" />

[[Out Of Commission]] and [[Who's Scruffy-Looking?]] are early interrupts that cancel named cards.<ref name="teching-ooc" /> They sit in the 60-card deck. [[Sense]] or [[Alter]] can cancel them in turn.<ref name="teching-sense" />

== Mother May I ==
[[Sense]] cancels an Interrupt or a React. [[Alter]] cancels an Effect. [[Control]], from [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]], cancels Sense and Alter.<ref name="teching-sense" /><ref name="teching-control" /> Colson said players called Sense, Alter and Control "Mother May I" cards.<ref name="colson-shields" /> [[Jerry Darcy]] later said he "utterly failed" his goal of avoiding permission decks such as Sense and Alter, and spent the rest of his time trying to fix that mistake.<ref name="darcy-pnh" />

Those universal counters can cancel a silver bullet that is not immune.<ref name="teching-sense" /> The Teching Overview calls that a fundamental design flaw of the early counters, which "should have been made immune to Sense and Alter".<ref name="teching-flaw" />

The [[Jedi Pack]] (April 1996) printed [[For Luck]] and [[Dark Forces]]. If Sense or Alter was just played, the owner may use X Force to exclude X Jedi or Dark Jedi from being the highest-ability character.<ref name="teching-jedi" />

[[A New Hope]] added grabbers: [[There'll Be Hell To Pay]], [[Tentacle]] and [[Grappling Hook]].<ref name="teching-grab" /> Premiere-only games are unbalanced without them.<ref name="teching-grab" />

Dagobah added [[Do, Or Do Not]] and [[There Is No Try]]. Sense and Alter become Lost Interrupts, and a successful destiny for them costs 2 Force.<ref name="dodn" /><ref name="teching-control" /> [[Special Edition]] Immediate Effects let a grabber play for free and send a canceled card to the Used Pile.<ref name="teching-se" /> [[Reflections II: Expanding the Galaxy]] printed combo cards that did both.<ref name="teching-se" />

== Building up a bullet ==
Decipher often started with a weak counter and later printed a harder one.<ref name="teching-build" />

[[Never Tell Me The Odds]] and [[3,720 To 1]] are insert cards.<ref name="teching-build" /><ref name="path-ban" /> [[Jabba's Palace]] then printed [[Ultimatum]] and [[Resistance]], which cap Force loss to an insert while the owner occupies battlegrounds.<ref name="teching-build" /> The same set printed [[Torture]] and [[Don't Forget The Droids]], which cancel those inserts as they are revealed and are immune to Sense.<ref name="teching-torture" /> [[Death Star II (expansion)|Death Star II]] printed [[Your Insight Serves You Well]] and [[You Cannot Hide Forever]] as Effects that start the game in play.<ref name="teching-insight" /><ref name="path-ban" />

[[Failure At The Cave]] and [[Broken Concentration]] are bullets against Jedi training decks.<ref name="teching-cave" /><ref name="path-obj" /> [[Ounee Ta]] and [[No Escape]], from [[Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck]], tax generic sites.<ref name="teching-ounee" /><ref name="path-obj" /> The Teching Overview says [[Ralltiir Operations]] mostly disappears once Ounee Ta is available.<ref name="teching-ounee" /> [[Come Here You Big Coward]] cancels [[Asteroid Sanctuary]] under most circumstances.<ref name="path-obj" /> [[Do They Have A Code Clearance?]] taxes Force retrieval.<ref name="teching-code" />

The same overview says [[Hidden Weapons]] and [[Fallen Portal]] had no dedicated Decipher counter besides Sense.<ref name="teching-hidden" />

== Crowding the sixty ==
Every silver bullet still occupies a slot in the 60-card deck.<ref name="colson-shields" /><ref name="teching-cons" /> Colson put the design problem this way: how to counter every really nasty deck and still have a deck that is fun to play, with the fun cards in it.<ref name="colson-shields" />

The Teching Overview lists the same cost. A bullet is wasted if the opponent is not on that strategy.<ref name="teching-cons" /> Sense and Alter limit early counters.<ref name="teching-cons" /> A bullet that is too strong can wipe out decks that would otherwise be fine.<ref name="teching-cons" /> Long cancel lists are confusing for new players.<ref name="teching-cons" /> The same overview says teching still keeps the game from settling on one best deck.<ref name="teching-cons" /> Decipher "got more direct with their silver bulleting over time."<ref name="teching-direct" />

== Defensive Shields ==
[[Reflections III: A Collector's Bounty]] (31 October 2001) printed the first [[Starting Effect]]s, [[Fear Is My Ally]] and [[An Unusual Amount Of Fear]].<ref name="ref3-rules" /> Each deploys before starting cards are revealed, with up to 10 cards from outside the deck face-down under it.<ref name="fima" /><ref name="auaof" /> Cards under the Starting Effect do not count toward the deck limit.<ref name="fima" /> The Starting Effect itself is the 60th card of the deck.<ref name="ref3-rules" /> Three times per game the owner may play a Defensive Shield from there as if from hand.<ref name="fima" />

Cards with the Gungan Warrior Shield icon are Defensive Shields.<ref name="ref3-rules" /> The rules supplement calls the pile "valuable additional defense against an opponent's nastier strategies" while sacrificing one slot of the 60-card deck.<ref name="ref3-rules" /> Replica titles of earlier Effects are a different card type. The unique and restricted rule still ties the Effect and the Shield together.<ref name="ref3-rules" />

Colson said that is where the side-deck concept came in with shields.<ref name="colson-shields" /> He called shields "a pretty in between solution."<ref name="colson-shields" /> He said other work was still needed "to either get to a second edition or something, but that became moot."<ref name="colson-shields" /> For the cancelled reboot pitch, see [[SWCCG 2nd Edition]].
